answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to pass a unique-compute check before it earns: the agent must complete a benchmark bound to its key that cannot be reused across clones, like quartz crystals that each form once under distinct pressure. A new identity starts as unproven jade, valuable only after repeated verified work, while an attacker who tries to forge many fake identities must pay full compute cost per clone, so mass fakery costs more than honest participation.
